Overview

Do US and Chinese AI models design websites differently?

—%

of our study sites were correctly identified as made by a US or a Chinese model, from their design measures alone.

80 study sites from the DGX Spark (US: Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss 120B; China: Qwen 3.8 27B, Qwen 3.5 122B) and 406 Arena sites from July 2026. Runs about — seconds.

Model origin

Chinese models’ sites are denser, with fewer images

Study sites, home pages. Chinese models’ average ÷ US models’ average across 40 matched pairs (same site type and prompt), log scale. Shown: the 10 largest of the measures that differ clearly (q < 0.05) and in the same direction for both model-size pairs.

Local details

Chinese models add local details without being asked

Share of study home pages (40 per side) whose visible text or labels include each item. Keyword checks; the matched text was saved and spot-checked (2 borderline hits of about 160).

Prompt language

Writing the prompt in Chinese changed almost nothing

Study sites. Measures (out of 40) that differ clearly: paired sign-flip test, Benjamini–Hochberg q < 0.05. Origin pairs share site type and prompt; language pairs share model and site type.

Identifiable

Origin can be read from our sites’ design, but barely from Arena’s

Logistic regression on the design measures, always tested on site types (study) or categories (Arena) left out of training. Chance is 50%.

Arena votes

With Chinese prompts, users chose Chinese models less often than expected

Arena WebDev votes, July 2026: US-vs-Chinese battles, Chinese prompts and a category-matched English sample, where both models have an official WebDev score (as of July 31, 2026). Expected share comes from the score gap.

Before concluding

What these results can and cannot say

  • One Chinese lab. Both Chinese models are Qwen (Alibaba), so “origin” may be Qwen’s house style. A second Chinese lab would separate the two.
  • Photos. The Qwen models often left placeholder boxes where photos go, which drives the image and color differences.
  • Automatic measures. They are first-pass instruments; a hand-coded sample would check them.
  • Arena’s template. Every Arena site starts from the same React template, and its prompts are mostly apps and games.
  • Next. Compare with real Chinese and US websites of the same types, then ask people.

Measurement code: arena/worker/page-measures.js and research/measures. Analysis: research/analysis/run_comparisons.py. 2 of 408 Arena sites could not be built.

We measured 40 design features on our 80 study sites and on 406 sites from Arena. This short walks through what differs, what does not, and how sure we are.

With Chinese prompts, Chinese models won — percent of votes. Their scores predicted about — percent. With English prompts the gap was smaller, and not clearly different from zero.

Both Chinese models come from one lab, so this may be Qwen’s style rather than a national one. Next, we compare with real websites, then ask people.
